s1.syndrome_frame: Acute coronary syndrome with recurrent chest pain and electrocardiographic changes
salient_findings: Paroxysmal chest pain occurring 5 times during the day
ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR on initial ECG
key_facts: Patient presented to the emergency department with chest pain
Chest pain was paroxysmal and occurred 5 times during the day
Each episode of chest pain lasted 15 to 30 minutes
Blood pressure was 106/52 mm Hg
Pulse rate was 64 beats per minute
Chest auscultation revealed normal breath and heart sounds with no murmurs
Hemogram, serum electrolyte levels, kidney and liver function tests, B-type natriuretic peptide and D-dimer levels were all within normal limits
Cardiac troponin I level was elevated at 25 ng/mL
Initial ECG revealed sinus rhythm, ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR, Q wave in lead III, and ST-segment depression in leads I, II, aVL, aVF, and V2 to V6
Repeated ECG showed sinus bradycardia, Q-wave amplitude deepening, ST-segment falling back to equipotential line, and T-wave inversion in lead III
Coronary angiography showed total occlusion of the right coronary artery and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated cardiac troponin I level and ECG changes consistent with myocardial infarction

shortlist.label: Right ventricular infarction
shortlist.why_kept: ECG changes in leads III and aVR, and total occlusion of the right coronary artery on coronary angiography

shortlist.label: Left main coronary artery disease
shortlist.why_kept: Subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery on coronary angiography

shortlist.label: Unstable angina
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent chest pain and electrocardiographic changes, with elevated cardiac troponin I level

shortlist.label: Variant angina
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent chest pain and electrocardiographic changes, with coronary artery spasm a possible cause

raw.rationale: Elevated cardiac troponin I level and ECG changes including ST-segment elevation and Q wave in lead III, along with total occlusion of the right coronary artery and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery on coronary angiography, are indicative of acute myocardial infarction.

rejected.label: Right ventricular infarction
rejected.why: While possible given the ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR, the total occlusion of the right coronary artery and involvement of other areas suggest a more extensive infarction pattern.

rejected.label: Left main coronary artery disease
rejected.why: Although subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery is present, the clinical and ECG findings more strongly suggest an acute myocardial infarction rather than just disease of the left main coronary artery.

rejected.label: Unstable angina
rejected.why: The presence of elevated cardiac troponin I and specific ECG changes indicate myocardial damage beyond what is typically seen in unstable angina.

rejected.label: Variant angina
rejected.why: The pattern of chest pain and ECG changes, along with the coronary angiography findings, do not align with the typical characteristics of variant angina, which usually involves transient coronary artery spasm without evidence of myocardial infarction.
